title: Sushi Rice
subtitle: Japanese vinegared rice for sushi
excerpt: The foundation of all sushi: short-grain Japanese rice cooked precisely, then folded while still hot with a mixture of rice vinegar, sugar, and salt until each grain is glossy, slightly sticky, and seasoned through. The rice is what makes sushi.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sushi rice is the central element of Japanese sushi, and making it correctly is considered a foundational skill in Japanese cooking; apprentice sushi chefs in Japan traditionally spend years mastering the rice before progressing to fish preparation. The rice used is Japanese short-grain, sometimes labelled sushi rice outside Japan. It must be washed until the water runs clear to remove surface starch, then cooked with slightly less water than usual. The seasoning vinegar mixture (su) is folded in with a fan to cool the rice rapidly while the starch is still active; this creates the characteristic glossy, slightly sticky texture. Using a wooden or bamboo vessel (hangiri or rice paddle in a large bowl) is traditional because wood absorbs excess moisture.

content.text: Wash the rice until the water runs completely clear; this step cannot be skipped or the rice will be sticky and gluey rather than having distinct grains that cling together. Fold the vinegar mixture in while the rice is still very hot and steam it; do not stir or the grains will break. Fan while folding to cool the rice as you season it.

items.preparation: use Japanese short-grain rice; washed in several changes of water until clear, then drained

content.text: Put the washed rice in a heavy saucepan with 400 ml of cold water. Bring to the boil, then immediately reduce to the lowest possible heat, cover tightly, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
While the rice cooks, gently heat the rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pan until dissolved. Leave to cool.

Turn the hot rice out into a large, wide bowl. Pour the vinegar mixture over it gradually, folding it in gently with a spatula or rice paddle using cutting and folding motions, never stirring. Fan the rice while folding to cool it. The rice should be glossy and slightly sticky. Use at room temperature; do not refrigerate or the grains will harden.
